_about: What belongs in the main product catalog and what goes to the secondary (discarded) list. Applies to the supermarket-style catalogs only (`applies_to`: snapshot keys starting with these prefixes); the wholesale sources (La Mayorista, Corabastos, USDA reports) are curated and always main. IN: fresh produce (vegetables, fruit, roots and tubers, fresh herbs), fresh / frozen meat, poultry, fish and seafood, processed meat that needs refrigeration or the cold chain (ham, bacon, sausage, deli meats, nuggets ...), cheese, eggs. OUT: every other dairy, canned or shelf-stable meat and fish (they travel by sea), frozen / canned / dried produce, nuts, rice and grains, flour, bakery, dough, sweets, drinks, sauces and condiments, spices, non-food. Name rules are regular expressions, case-insensitive, matched against the product name. The first matching `out` rule wins. Everything is editable here; a person's own choice (move to / from the secondary list) always wins over these rules.

keep_name._about: Cheese and eggs. With an HS code the code decides (heading 04: in; any other chapter: out, so 'Four Cheese mashed potatoes' or a 'ham and cheese pocket' are not cheese); with no HS code the `not` words guard against cheese-flavoured snacks and dishes.

cold_chain_meat._about: Processed meat that needs refrigeration or the cold chain stays in the main catalog (it travels by air). Canned / shelf-stable meat is caught by the `canned_shelf_stable` rule first. Applies when the HS code is meat / fish (02, 03, 16) or missing; a conflicting code (bakery, preparations) defers to the HS rules.
